title: Founding Biocon in a garage
statement: Mazumdar Shaw started Biocon as an enzymes venture in a Bangalore garage at 25, after being denied brewing jobs in Australia because she was a woman — with Rs 10,000 and a rented space.
outcome: Biocon became India's largest biopharmaceutical company, moved from enzymes to statins to biosimilars, and its founder became the face of Indian science entrepreneurship.

title: The statins pivot — from enzymes to biopharma
statement: Mazumdar Shaw committed the company to fermentation-based statin production at scale, competing with global pharma at price points they would not match.
outcome: Biocon's statins made it the world's largest producer of several cholesterol molecules, funded the move into biosimilars, and made the 2004 IPO among India's most successful pharma listings.

title: Biosimilars and the $3.3 billion... actually the 2022 Biocon Biologics Viatris deal
statement: Biocon Biologics agreed to acquire Viatris's biosimilars business for roughly $3.3 billion, betting that biosimilar scale would be the industry's consolidation endgame.
outcome: The acquisition made Biocon Biologics one of the world's largest biosimilars players with full control of its global commercial infrastructure.
